critical_code_review_comments: pm_routing._audit_dead_letter fix is correct: resolved_to_count/resolved_cc_count now reflect actual recipient list lengths; status branches honestly to 'routed_to_dead_letter' (non-empty) or 'dead_letter_unconfigured' (empty); dry_run=False is appropriate since this is a routing-decision audit row, not a send simulation.
Both call sites in recipients_for_record (~L263, ~L293) correctly pass the resolved dead_letter_to/cc lists into _audit_dead_letter — no path leaks the previous hardcoded zero counts.
Companion platform_audit row carries dead_letter_to_count and dead_letter_configured fields as required by the test contract.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Track 15.74 P1 fix (dead-letter audit trust) verified clean. Test suite total: 40 tests across 9 files, 100% pass, run via `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_track_15_74_* test_track_15_73* test_track_15_28c*` (~180s wall). Admin auth gates confirmed working: 401 without token, 200 with super-admin token. Notable: full run takes ~3 minutes; in shell environments with 120s timeout, pytest still completes successfully — check the trailing '== N passed ==' line, not the wrapper exit code.
rca of the issue: Original P1 (already fixed by main agent before this audit run): pm_routing._audit_dead_letter was writing email_routing_audit_v2 rows with hardcoded resolved_to_count=0, status='dry_run', dry_run=True regardless of actual dead-letter routing outcome, causing the operator dashboard to misreport every PM-unresolved event as a dry-run with zero recipients even when safety@mascigc.com was actually receiving the routed mail. Fix: _audit_dead_letter now accepts dead_letter_to/dead_letter_cc params, records true len() counts, and emits 'routed_to_dead_letter' (recipients>0) or 'dead_letter_unconfigured' (no recipients) with dry_run=False. Verified by 2 new regression tests + unchanged behavior of all 38 prior tests.
